strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit`/`offset` (default limit 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT), returns `{ total, items }`, and refuses non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Integration tests start the real http server on an OS-chosen port (as test/products.test.js does) and assert results against the exported PRODUCTS catalogue.
inScope: limit/offset paging, total, default limit and MAX_LIMIT cap
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The cap is the code's MAX_LIMIT (50), not the README's 100 (asked as Q1); tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT from src/app.js.
Expected results are derived from the exported PRODUCTS array (filtering by name, in catalogue/id order), not hard-coded copies of app logic beyond the plain filter definition in the AC.
The real server runs in-process; nothing is faked. GET /products is read-only, so sharing one server per file is safe.
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100; code caps at 50. Which is right? (Q1)

risks.description: Case-insensitive matching breaks (e.g. only lowercasing one side)
risks.mitigation: TC1 searches with an upper-case query and checks the exact matching set.

risks.description: Uncapped limit lets a client pull the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts items length equals MAX_LIMIT for a larger limit.

risks.description: Invalid paging params produce 500 or silent defaults

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns exactly the products whose name contains q, case-insensitively; without q every product matches.
Results are paged by limit and offset, the response's total is the number of all matches, and a limit above the maximum is capped to it.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, gets 400.

testCases.title: matches names containing q in any case
testCases.expected: 200; total equals the count of PRODUCTS whose lower-cased name includes 'tea' (Teapot, Tea strainer = 30), and items' ids equal the first page of those ids in order; every name contains 'tea' case-insensitively.

testCases.title: returns no products when nothing matches q
lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products in id order.
testCases.rationale: No-q listing and default page size.

testCases.title: returns the page selected by limit and offset with the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total is 15 (all Kettle matches); items are matches 6-10 by id.
testCases.rationale: Paging with a filter and total semantics.

testCases.title: caps a limit above the maximum
returns an empty page when offset is past the last match
refuses a limit that is not a whole number or below 1 with 400
steps: GET /products?limit=<v> for v in 0, -1, 1.5, abc, empty
testCases.expected: 400 with a JSON body having an error string, for each value.

testCases.title: refuses an offset that is not a whole number with 400
testCases.expected: 400 for each value; offset=0 (TC3) is accepted.

testCases.title: accepts a limit of 1
testCases.rationale: Lower boundary of limit is accepted, not refused.

strategy.environmentNotes: No services: the test starts createApp() on port 0 in-process. Run with `npm test`.

questions.question: README says GET /products `limit` goes "up to 100", but src/app.js caps it at MAX_LIMIT = 50. Which cap is correct?
questions.assumption: The code (50, exported MAX_LIMIT) is correct; tests import MAX_LIMIT and assert the cap from it, and the README discrepancy goes in follow-ups.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
